idea: Independent AI tooling evaluation and procurement advisory
buyer: COOs and heads of research choosing between AI vendors
pain: Vendor claims are unverifiable and procurement decisions are expensive
v1: One comparative evaluation for one firm's use case
channel: Her network and her AI-adoption reputation
verdict: Genuinely useful and well-timed, but it is a one-off purchase per firm with an obvious conflict question.

why.distribution: 20-50 warm firms, and this is precisely what her AI-adoption reputation signals she can do.
why.demand: Firms are making these decisions now with poor information; nobody has been quoted.
why.fmf: Evaluating LLM tooling for a sceptical professional firm is literally her former remit.
why.revenue_structure: One-off per procurement cycle, which recurs only every year or two.
why.defensibility: Accumulated comparative evaluations become a genuine asset if she publishes them.
why.leverage: Evaluation frameworks and prior comparisons carry over between clients.
why.tailwind: Procurement decisions are happening across the whole sector right now.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 evaluations = £198k, requiring 18 firms in procurement in one year.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 evaluations = £198k. Procurement cycles are infrequent per firm, so 18 evaluations means 18 different firms in one year - a marketing problem, not a delivery one. Realistic: 5-7 = £55-77k.
carries: Exact fit with her reputation, high tailwind, and an accumulating comparison dataset if she publishes.
kills: No repeat within a client, so every pound needs a new firm in a buying window.
test: Ask five firms whether they are choosing an AI tool this year and would pay for independent evaluation.
test_pass: Two are mid-decision and ask for a proposal.
test_fail: They rely on vendor trials and peer recommendations.
